title: Prediction of 10 km running time by physical and training characteristics in recreational runners
authors: Suwankan S, Suwankan S, Theanthong A, Kemarat S
journal: Journal of Human Sport and Exercise
population: Recreational runners who ran 10 km on a track and reported training characteristics
findings: 10 km time correlated with training distance (r = -0.605), training days (r = -0.583), training duration (r = -0.446), running experience (r = -0.275), mini-marathon races entered (r = -0.311) and BMI (r = 0.275).
These variables predicted 57% of the variance in 10 km time.
Weekly training distance showed the greatest effect on running time.
The authors conclude that more weekly distance and more training days give a shorter 10 km time.
limitations: Crossref abstract only; full text not read. Self-reported training, correlational, n = 60. Longest run was not among the reported predictors.
implications: For 10 km, weekly volume and training frequency are the reported correlates of performance; raise weekly time and run days before lengthening the long run.
No evidence in this study that a longer long run improves 10 km time independently of weekly volume (the variable was not examined).
